notes: syscall: linux/amd64 constants, struct layouts and zsyscall wrappers generated by tools/gen_syscall.go from Go's own sources into rust_stdlib_sys::syscall; hand-written helpers port the rest. System calls run for real on linux/x86_64 (extern "C" syscall from the C library); other targets get the portable libc subset (read, write, close, dup, fsync, ftruncate, the id and process queries, umask, wait4, fork/exec) and ENOSYS for the rest. Errno and Signal use the Linux tables on every host. Names are snake_case functions and SCREAMING constants; Go struct names are kept (Stat_t, RawSockaddrInet4). Go's int is isize, uint and uintptr are usize, string is &str, []byte is &[u8] or &mut [u8], pointers are references (Option for nil-able ones). Wrappers return Result<T, Errno> and drop Go's raw result on failure.

AllThreadsSyscall.note: Go's runtime stops every thread and runs the call on each; Rust has no such runtime, so the call runs on the calling thread only. Setuid, Setgid and the other id setters use the C library, which does synchronise all threads.

BytePtrFromString.note: Go returns a *byte into a fresh []byte; Rust returns the owned, NUL-terminated std::ffi::CString (as_ptr gives the pointer). The error cases (EINVAL for an embedded NUL) match.

Conn.note: Any socket or file with a descriptor (std's AsRawFd) is a Conn; net::syscall_conn turns it into a RawConn.

ForkLock.note: A std::sync::RwLock<()>; Go's sync.RWMutex has the same read/write locking shape.

InotifyEvent.note: #[repr(C)] with C's layout: 16 bytes (SizeofInotifyEvent). gc's unsafe.Sizeof reports 20 because it pads a struct that ends in a zero-length array; the field offsets are identical.

ParseNetlinkRouteAttr.note: Returns EINVAL where Go panics (slice bounds out of range) when a message is shorter than its fixed header.

SlicePtrFromStrings.note: Go returns []*byte; Rust returns a CStringVec that owns the strings and exposes the NUL-terminated pointer array through as_ptr.

Stderr.note: A constant: Go's Stderr is a variable that is never reassigned in practice.

Stdin.note: A constant: Go's Stdin is a variable that is never reassigned in practice.

Stdout.note: A constant: Go's Stdout is a variable that is never reassigned in practice.

StringBytePtr.note: Deprecated. Returns an owned std::ffi::CString instead of a *byte; panics on an embedded NUL as Go does.

StringSlicePtr.note: Deprecated. Returns a CStringVec instead of []*byte; panics on an embedded NUL as Go does.

SysProcAttr.GidMappings.note: An empty Vec is Go's nil: no mapping is written.

SysProcAttr.PidFD.note: An Option<Arc<AtomicIsize>> in place of *int: the cell receives the pidfd, or -1, and the caller owns the descriptor.

SysProcAttr.UidMappings.note: An empty Vec is Go's nil: no mapping is written. Go's non-nil empty slice would still synchronise with the child and write nothing.
